data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Rules 90 and 184 reach a cycle of length at most 2 within 4*W steps for all W between 5 and 11, whereas Rule 110 does not for any width in this range. The structural property separating them is that Rule 90 is a linear (additive) rule over GF(2), ensuring the state space decomposes into independent subspaces with transient lengths bounded by the matrix nilpotency (at most W), and Rule 184 is a conservative, monotonic particle-conserving rule where the number of 01 and 10 boundaries strictly decreases until reaching a fixed point or 2-cycle. Rule 110 lacks both properties, possessing nonlinear interactions that support gliders and chaotic attractors. Consequently, Rule 54 (which is also nonlinear and lacks monotonicity/conservation) is predicted to fail this criterion for all W in 5..11.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If a width-W configuration of Rule 90 with wrap-around exhibits a transient longer than W (contradicting the GF(2) nilpotency bound), the claim fails.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If Rule 184 exhibits a transient longer than W/2 or a cycle longer than 2 for any W in 5..11, the monotonic boundary-decrease mechanism is falsified.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If Rule 110 reaches a cycle of length <= 2 within 4*W steps for all 2^W states across all W in 5..11, the claim regarding Rule 110's structural complexity is falsified.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If Rule 54 reaches a cycle of length <= 2 within 4*W steps for all states across all W in 5..11, the prediction that nonlinear non-conservative rules fail this criterion is overturned.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Rule 90 computes the XOR of left and right neighbors. This linearity over GF(2) restricts the maximum transient length to the nilpotency index of its transition matrix, which cannot exceed W. Thus, it falls well within 4*W. Rule 184 conserves the number of '1's and acts as a deterministic traffic flow model. The number of alternating boundaries (0110 patterns) strictly decreases over time, bounding the transient by W/2 and inevitably leading to a 1-cycle (blocked traffic) or 2-cycle (moving traffic). Rule 110 is nonlinear and capable of universal computation, exhibiting gliders that collide stochastically, yielding arbitrarily long transients and cycles >2. Rule 54 exhibits similar nonlinear, non-conservative glider interactions, so its transient length is expected to exceed 4*W for some initial states.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
